newsitem.title: USA: Calif. welfare fraud costs $590 mln a year - state.
newsitem.headline: Calif. welfare fraud costs $590 mln a year - state.

text.p: Welfare fraud in California may cost taxpayers nearly $590 million a year, according to a state study released on Wednesday.
The welfare fraud study, conducted in Orange County, found that a third of the recipients receiving cash and food stamp assistance are receiving the benefits fraudulently.

In Orange County alone, nearly $23 million a year is unnecessarily paid out because of welfare fraud to recipients of Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC) and food stamps, California's Health and Welfare Agency said.
When these results are expanded statewide, the agency estimated that nearly $590 million may be lost to fraud on a yearly basis.

"This is an outrage," said state Health and Welfare Secretary Sandra Smoley. "In an era of limited resources, it is beyond belief to think that $590 million in taxpayers dollars that could have been spent on services for the truly needy went to greedy people out to defraud the system."
The most prevalent type of fraud found in the study was unreported income obtained through the underground economy, the agency said.
The study was conducted by the California Department of Social Services in conjunction with the Orange County Social Services Agency and the Orange County District Attorney's Office.

A total of 450 cases were investigated between August 1994 and October 1995. Of those, 201 cases were found to have provided false eligibility information to county welfare officials. Of those, 134 received money they were not entitled to.
